summary: This note is an overview of Nanjing, the capital of Jiangsu province in China's lower Yangtze region. It covers the city's long history as a capital of dynasties and republican governments, from prehistoric "Nanjing Man" to the Nanjing Massacre and the Republic of China. It also covers geography, population, economy, transport, education, culture, museums, sports and tourism.
one_line: Overview of Nanjing, Jiangsu's capital and one of China's Four Great Ancient Capitals, covering its history, geography, economy, culture and infrastructure.
key_facts: Nanjing (南京) means "Southern Capital" and is the capital of Jiangsu province and the second largest city in East China, with a total population of 8,216,100.

Nanjing is recognized as one of the Four Great Ancient Capitals of China and served as capital of Eastern Wu (211-280), the Eastern Jin and Southern Dynasties (317-589), the Southern Tang (937-76), the Ming dynasty (1368-1421) and the Republic of China (1927–37, 1945–49).
Nanjing first became a state capital in 229 AD, when Sun Quan's state of Eastern Wu relocated its capital to Jianye.
In 317 the Jin court fled south and re-established itself in Nanjing, then called Jiankang, the first time the national capital moved to the south.
When Qing forces led by Zeng Guofan retook the city from the Taiping in 1864, over 100,000 people are estimated to have committed suicide or fought to the death.

The first Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge was begun in 1960 and opened in 1968; it is a two-tiered road and rail bridge spanning 4,600 metres on the upper deck, built and designed by the Chinese themselves.
As of October 2014, Nanjing had five bridges and two tunnels over the Yangtze River.
In 2013 Nanjing's GDP was RMB 801 billion (3rd in Jiangsu), with GDP per capita of RMB 98,174 (US$16041), up 11 percent from 2012.
Nanjing has a total land area of 6,598 square kilometres and lies 300 km west-northwest of Shanghai and 1,200 km south-southeast of Beijing.
According to the Sixth China Census, Nanjing's population reached 8.005 million in 2010; the Han make up 98.56 percent of residents and the Hui are the largest minority.

Nanjing has 75 institutions of higher learning as of 2013, and its number of National key laboratories and academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Chinese Academy of Engineering ranks third in the nation.
Nanjing Museum, formerly the National Central Museum, holds 400,000 items and has one of the world's largest collections of Ming and Qing imperial porcelain.
The Xinhai Revolution led to the founding of the Republic of China in January 1912 with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president and Nanking as capital, but Yuan Shikai demanded the capital be Beijing.
Wutaishan Sports Center was established in 1952, and Jiangsu Sainty football club is a long-term tenant of Nanjing Olympic Sports Center.
